syntheticBoundary.simulationNotice: This is simulated feedback from a configured audience lens, not real user research.

lenses.label: Target User Comprehension Lens
lenses.purpose: Stress-test whether a likely target user can understand the offer, audience, outcome, and next step after one pass.
assumptions: The user has the job context named in the brief
The user has not received a sales explanation outside the supplied copy
reviewQuestions: Can the reader name what the product or offer is?
Can the reader name who it is for?
Can the reader name the practical next step?
safetyRules: Do not infer market preference
Do not claim real readers will understand
Recommend a comprehension test when uncertainty remains
lenses.recommendedValidation: Ask five target users to read the first sentence and describe what the product is, who it is for, and what action they would take next.

lenses.label: Technical Evaluator Proof Lens
lenses.purpose: Stress-test whether proof, caveats, and technical claims are inspectable without overstating certainty.
assumptions: The evaluator is skeptical of unsupported performance, security, integration, and reliability claims
The evaluator expects tradeoffs and limits to be visible
reviewQuestions: Which claims would require proof before belief?
Which words sound like unsupported authority or certainty?
Are limitations and caveats visible enough?
safetyRules: Do not invent proof
Mark unsupported claims as blocked_unsupported
Require source or evidence ids for material claims
lenses.recommendedValidation: Have a qualified evaluator review the claim/proof map and mark which claims are believable, missing proof, or require expert review.

lenses.label: Executive Sponsor Relevance Lens
lenses.purpose: Stress-test whether the message states a credible business problem, practical value, and decision path without hype.
assumptions: The sponsor needs relevance, risk, and next-step clarity
reviewQuestions: What business problem is this solving?
What decision or next step is being requested?
What proof would be needed before sponsoring the next step?
safetyRules: Use unclear time relevance instead of low urgency
Do not create fake urgency
Tie recommendations to evidence or testable hypotheses
lenses.recommendedValidation: Ask target sponsors what decision they think the copy is asking for and what proof they would need before agreeing to the next step.

lenses.label: First-Time Reader Clarity Lens
lenses.purpose: Stress-test plain-English understandability for readers with limited prior context.
assumptions: The reader will not work hard to resolve pronouns, acronyms, or vague references
reviewQuestions: Which terms require prior context?
Which pronouns or references are ambiguous?
Can the reader summarize the message in one sentence?
safetyRules: Do not downgrade necessary technical terms automatically
Recommend explanation when a term is essential
Do not claim non-target clarity equals target-user usefulness
lenses.recommendedValidation: Run a five-minute comprehension test with target users after plain-language issues are fixed.

lenses.label: Anxiety-Reduction Accessibility Lens
lenses.purpose: Reduce intimidation and pressure while preserving reader agency, clear risk, and access to support or expert review when needed.
assumptions: Some readers may feel pressure, confusion, or concern when risk, eligibility, or consequence language is unclear
The message should clarify choices without exploiting anxiety
reviewQuestions: Does the copy preserve user control?
Does it clarify risk without exaggerating fear?
Does it avoid urgency, shame, and status pressure?
Does it recommend support or expert review when the domain requires it?
safetyRules: Clarify risk
Preserve user control
Reduce pressure
Avoid urgency and status language
Recommend safer support or expert review when needed
blockedUses: manipulative persuasion aimed at minors or vulnerable people
lenses.recommendedValidation: Ask target readers whether the copy makes the choice, risk, and support path clearer without creating pressure to act.

lenses.label: Specialist Bandwidth Lens
lenses.purpose: Stress-test whether organization-facing documentation respects scarce specialist attention, preserves expert autonomy, and reaches usable action before asking the reader to learn a new framework.
assumptions: The reader may be highly specialized and already carrying high cognitive load
The reader will resist generic onboarding, remedial framing, vague process language, and unnecessary learning tax
The document must preserve technical precision while making the fastest useful path obvious
reviewQuestions: Can the specialist reach a useful answer or action before learning a new framework?
Does the document preserve expert agency instead of sounding remedial or bureaucratic?
Are exact terms, caveats, and evidence boundaries visible enough for a technical reader to trust?
Does the page create reading momentum by making the next useful step obvious?
Which section would a busy specialist skip, resist, or challenge?
safetyRules: Do not call readers entitled, difficult, lazy, or resistant
Do not remove necessary technical precision to chase simplicity
Do not frame reading momentum as addiction or dependency
Keep synthetic feedback separate from employee research
Recommend task-based validation before claiming adoption or performance impact
lenses.recommendedValidation: Ask specialists to use the document for a real task and measure skim-to-answer time, follow-up questions, task completion, skipped sections, trust objections, and whether the document felt respectful and useful.

validationRules.message: Audience lens output must be marked as not market evidence.
Audience lenses must include review questions.
Use anxiety-reduction accessibility lens instead of anxious first-time user.
Synthetic reader output cannot be treated as user validation.
